doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Black Chicago youth bands, and his mother teaching Nat Cole
summary: Hinton describes how young musicians from different schools met, the Chicago Defender youth band, and his mother teaching piano to Nat Cole and his brother Eddie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Ray Nance, Lionel Hampton. You know what was so wonderful about that it was a black community, and we didn’t all go to the same school, but we all met musically. So with bands, like, you went to some school, I went to Winifred, but we had rehearsals, and then after hours, we met, and that’s how we got to know each other. And to see all of that going on, we had Clark Smith and the Chicago Defender, the newspaper, hired Basie and Clark Smith to start a youth band, and that’s where we came in. My mother was Nat Cole’s piano teacher. See my mother played for Nat’s father, had a church on Dearborn Street, one of those storefront churches, and my mother was the organist, piano player for the church, and for the BYPU, so she had Nat there. He was always a nice guy. You know I was always getting in trouble, and my mom would say, “Why can’t you be nice like Nathaniel?” And I couldn’t stand him. ‘Cause as kids, we really thought what we’d like to see was his big brother, Eddie.
